title: Complexe de De Rham à puissance divisée [conférence de 1976 à l’IHÉS] : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
The page is a scratch computation on the back of a mimeographed page of SGA 7 IX (Néron models); the neighbouring 'pages' are that printed text and are mathematically unrelated. The mathematics belongs to the divided-power (PD) de Rham project of the 1976 IHÉS talk.

Setup. k is a base ring (in the header Z: 'Z-algèbre'), and k{...} denotes PD polynomial algebras.
- A_1 = k{X0,X1,dX0,dX1}/(d(X0+X1)) with X0+X1 = T. This is the PD de Rham complex of the 'homogeneous 1-simplex' {X0+X1 = T}, relative to the PD line k{T}.
- Concretely A_1 = k{T}{X0,dX0} ≅ k{T}{X1,dX1}. Degree 0 is k{T}{X0}, degree 1 is k{T}{X0}dX0, and d is k{T}-linear with d(X0^{(i)}) = X0^{(i-1)}dX0.
- A_0 = k{T}. The two face maps α, β: A_1 → A_0 are the restrictions to the endpoints: α puts X0 = 0 (so X1 = T), β puts X0 = T (so X1 = 0), and both kill dX0.
- This is the start of a semi-simplicial differential PD algebra A_* (presumably A_n = PD de Rham complex of {X0+...+Xn = T} over k{T}). It is a PD, integral analogue of Sullivan's simplicial polynomial forms, with the simplex coned by a parameter T instead of Σt_i = 1.

Problem. Determine the endomorphisms of A_*. On this page he finds the conditions on the degree-1 component φ_1, subject to compatibility with the faces (α∘φ_1 = α, β∘φ_1 = β).
- Put ξ_i = φ_1(X0^{(i)}).
- (1) The PD relations: ξ_iξ_j = c_ij ξ_{i+j}, with c_ij = binom(i+j,i).
- φ_1(dX0) = dξ_1; he notes dξ_1 must commute with all ξ_i since A_1 is commutative.
- (2) Compatibility with d: dξ_i = ξ_{i-1}dξ_1 for i ≥ 2, and also on 1-forms, d(ξ_i dξ_1) = φ_1(0) = 0.
- (3a) α(ξ_i) = 0 and (3b) β(ξ_i) = T^{(i)}.

Computation.
- Write ξ_i = A_i + B_i dX0, with A_i = Σ_{j≥0} a_ij X0^{(j)}, B_i = Σ_{j≥0} b_ij X0^{(j)}, and a_ij, b_ij ∈ k{T}. He allows a possible odd component.
- (3a) gives a_{i0} = 0, i.e. A_i = Σ_{j≥1} a_ij X0^{(j)}.
- (3b) gives Σ_{j≥1} a_ij T^{(j)} = T^{(i)}.
- Then dξ_i = (Σ_{j≥1} a_ij X0^{(j-1)})dX0, since B_i dX0 is closed (top degree, T-coefficients closed).
- Also ξ_{i-1}dξ_1 = (Σ_k a_1k X0^{(k-1)})(Σ_k a_{i-1,k} X0^{(k)})dX0, the B-part dying because (dX0)^2 = 0.
- Equating these two gives a recursion for the a_ij. The page stops before solving it; one expects the endomorphisms to be essentially forced (rigidity of A_*, e.g. only the identity plus T-rescalings).

Purpose. Presumably to show that the cosimplicial PD de Rham object, used to compare PD de Rham cohomology with cochains or to build functorial integral 'Sullivan-type' models, has essentially no nontrivial automorphisms, so comparison maps are canonical.
errors: The relation defining A_1 is transcribed/appears as (dX0 - dX1). For X0+X1 = T with T a closed parameter (dT = 0), and for the identification A_1 = k{T}{X0,dX0} used afterwards, it must be d(X0+X1) = dX0 + dX1. With a minus sign, dT = 2dX0 ≠ 0.
Allowing an odd component B_i dX0 in ξ_i = φ_1(X0^{(i)}) is unnecessary if φ_1 is required to preserve degree; the B_i then vanish. Harmless, since the B-terms drop out of all computed conditions.

The computation is unfinished. The final equation comparing dξ_i with ξ_{i-1}dξ_1 (a recursion on the a_ij) is set up but not solved, and the analysis of the 1-form condition d(ξ_i dξ_1) = 0 is only sketched.

ideas.what: A semi-simplicial commutative differential PD algebra A_*, whose levels are PD de Rham complexes of 'simplices' X0+...+Xn = T over the PD line k{T}, with face maps given by restriction to coordinate faces.
ideas.modern_name: Simplicial PD polynomial de Rham forms (integral analogue of Sullivan's ∇(•,*) / Cartan's simplicial dga's); cf. integral de Rham models of Cenkl–Porter
ideas.usually_credited_to: Sullivan (1977) and H. Cartan (1976) over Q; integral/tame versions by Cenkl–Porter (c. 1980–81); PD de Rham complexes by Berthelot/Grothendieck (crystalline theory)
ideas.where_published: Not in published texts; the 1976 IHÉS talk on the PD de Rham complex seems unpublished (unsure)

ideas.what: Computation of endomorphisms of this cosimplicial PD dga compatible with faces: PD relations ξ_iξ_j = binom(i+j,i)ξ_{i+j}, d-compatibility dξ_i = ξ_{i-1}dξ_1, and endpoint conditions Σ a_ij T^{(j)} = T^{(i)}.
ideas.modern_name: Rigidity / automorphism computation of a cosimplicial model of cochains

ideas.what: Homogenized simplex X0+X1 = T with T a free PD parameter, instead of the affine simplex Σ t_i = 1.
ideas.modern_name: Coned/graded simplices; PD affine line as base

missed.claim: Grothendieck sets up the determination of endomorphisms of the semi-simplicial PD de Rham algebra A_* (homogeneous simplices X0+...+Xn = T over k{T}), deriving explicit constraints on φ_1, but does not finish. This bears on whether integral PD analogues of Sullivan's polynomial forms are rigid, i.e. whether comparison with cochains is canonical.
missed.quote: Endomorphismes de la Z-algèbre différentielles semi-simpliciale A_* ... ξ_i ξ_j = c_ij ξ_{i+j} ... dξ_i = ξ_{i-1} dξ_1 ... Σ_{j≥1} a_ij T^{(j)} = T^{(i)}
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: Integral and p-adic models of cochains (Mandell's E∞ models, Cenkl–Porter, recent work on PD/'binomial' de Rham models and derived de Rham) need functorial simplicial dga-type objects. An early Grothendieck attempt at a PD simplicial de Rham model over Z, with T-homogenized simplices, is a historically notable precursor, though only sketched here.

deep.surprise_reason: Routine but interesting: evidence that around 1975–76 Grothendieck was building an integral divided-power analogue of the simplicial polynomial de Rham algebra (with a T-homogenized simplex) and studying its endomorphisms. This predates or parallels Sullivan and Cartan and the integral versions. The page itself is only an unfinished elementary computation.
transcription_corrections: The relation in A_1 should read d(X0+X1) = dX0 + dX1 (consistent with X0+X1 = T and A_1 = k{T}{X0,dX0}), not dX0 - dX1.
Second line: 'k{T}{X0, dX0} = k{T}{X1, dX1}' (the struck item is a miswritten dX0).
Header: 'Endomorphismes de la Z-algèbre différentielle semi-simpliciale A_*'.
Marginal note: roughly 'bil. A bien à cause ...; il faut aussi que dξ_1 commute avec ξ_i (i≥1) en A_1 commutative!'.
c_ij is the PD binomial coefficient binom(i+j, i).
